label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey = Integer.toString(randNumber) where randNumber = new java.util.Random().nextInt(99). java.util.Random is a predictable PRNG, and rememberMeKey is used as a cookie value (set via response.addCookie(rememberMe)) and stored in the session (request.getSession().setAttribute(cookieName, rememberMeKey)). Using insecure randomness for authentication/session-related cookies is a real vulnerability. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-FP — resolved sink values are rememberMe.getName() = cookieName (derived from class name substring, fully server-controlled) and rememberMe.getValue() = rememberMeKey (derived from java.util.Random, not user input). Although the scanner traces cookie.getValue() as a source, the cookie referenced in the sink (rememberMe) is freshly created in this function with server-generated values, not the user-controlled cookie parsed earlier into param/bar. User input (from the decoded cookie value assigned to param) does not reach the response.getWriter().println sink. Case TP: Alert 1 is alert-TP.

evidence.note: java.util.Random().nextInt(99) produces predictable random number assigned to randNumber, then converted to rememberMeKey
rememberMeKey (from insecure Random) used as cookie value and stored in session attribute — security-sensitive context
